items.stem: A stakeholder says 'just add a new button to the screen.' What should a business analyst do first?

options.text: Understand the underlying problem the button is meant to solve
options.rationale: Correct: BAs analyse the need before accepting a stated solution.

options.text: Immediately document 'add a button' as the requirement
options.rationale: This records a solution, not the underlying business need.
The request is a useful starting point, not something to reject.

options.text: Escalate to senior management without analysis
options.rationale: Escalation is premature before the need is understood.

items.explanation: Correct: BAs analyse the need before accepting a stated solution.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which are qualities of a well-written requirement? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: a requirement must be verifiable against a clear criterion.

options.text: It is traceable to a business need
options.rationale: Correct: traceability shows why the requirement exists.

options.text: It specifies the exact screen layout
options.rationale: That is design detail, not a business requirement.

options.text: It is deliberately vague to allow flexibility
options.rationale: Vagueness makes a requirement untestable and ambiguous.

items.explanation: Correct: a requirement must be verifiable against a clear criterion.

items.stem: A BA builds an elaborate data model that no stakeholder question actually needed. What principle is violated?

options.text: Model to answer a question, not for its own sake
options.rationale: Correct: models are tools to answer specific questions, not decoration.

options.text: Always build the most detailed model possible
options.rationale: Detail without purpose wastes effort and obscures insight.

options.text: Data models are never appropriate in BA work
options.rationale: Data models are valid when they answer a real question.
Models are often shared with stakeholders to confirm understanding.

items.explanation: Correct: models are tools to answer specific questions, not decoration.
